name: Wood Ear: deep black
summary: Bright, blue-heavy light during fruiting for the near-black ears prized in cold salads and hot pots.
notes: Color builds over the stage. Ears grown dim come out brown.
chamber_notes: Bright LEDs add heat; check that the chamber does not run warm. Chamber limits: there is no heater or cooler, so temperature targets only hold if the room sits near them. There is no CO2 sensor, so the fan schedule stands in for fresh air. The humidifier can only add moisture, so a low humidity target depends on dry room air.

source_notes.title: Qiu et al. 2023, wood ear light intensity
source_notes.detail: Cells 12(1):56, 2023. A. heimuer fruits grew darker as light rose from 10 to 500 umol per m2 per s, with the most melanin at the highest level.

source_notes.title: Agriculture 2026, wood ear blue light
source_notes.detail: Agriculture 16(19):2167, 2026. Melanin build-up in A. heimuer was tied to blue light treatment.

source_notes.title: Stamets
source_notes.detail: Paul Stamets, Growing Gourmet and Medicinal Mushrooms (commonly cited chamber ranges). Auricularia spp. fruit warm (often 20 to 30 °C) at 85 to 95% humidity.

light_recipe.why: 65% white is about 2,400 lux plus full blue. Darker ears came with more light in Qiu 2023 and with blue light in the 2026 study. The chamber is far below the top intensity in Qiu 2023, so this is the brightest practical setting, not a match.
light_recipe.wavelength_note: WS2812 red is roughly 620 to 630 nm and blue roughly 465 to 475 nm. The RGB mix is an approximation of the cited wavelengths, not a measured spectrum. RGB percent is LED drive level, not a photon ratio.
